note: Typical factory specs. Confirm with the service manual, owner's manual or under-hood label before torquing or filling.

engines.name: GM Vortec V8 (Gen III: 4.8, 5.3, 6.0)
engines.checked: Oil, fuel pressure, plug gap and oil pressure checked against the factory manual (2004 Silverado 2500 6.0)
specs: 6 psi at 1,000 rpm, 18 psi at 2,000, 24 psi at 4,000
Odd (1, 3, 5, 7) on the driver side front to back, even (2, 4, 6, 8) on the passenger side
Current plug ACDelco 41-985 (iridium) comes gapped at 0.040 in; don't regap it. The original platinum plugs were 0.060 in (GM bulletin 03-06-04-060B)
At the lower radiator hose, on the water pump
About 55 to 62 psi, key on engine off
Behind the intake manifold at the top rear of the engine. A common oil leak and the usual cause of a jumping oil gauge
Under the intake manifold in the valley (codes P0327 / P0332); the intake has to come off
Rear bolts often break, causing a tick at cold start that fades when warm

engines.name: GM Vortec V8 (Gen IV: 4.8, 5.3, 6.0, 6.2)
engines.checked: Oil, plug gap, plug torque and fuel pressure checked against the factory manual (2007 Silverado 1500 5.3)
specs: Odd (1, 3, 5, 7) on the driver side front to back, even (2, 4, 6, 8) on the passenger side
At the lower radiator hose, on the water pump
50 to 60 psi, key on engine off
Most 5.3s (and some 6.0/6.2) have AFM. Collapsed lifters and oil burning are common; keep the oil full and changed on time
Top rear of the engine behind the intake. Leaks and false low readings are common (a screen under the sensor can clog too)
Rear bolts often break, causing a tick at cold start

engines.name: GM 6.0 V8 (HD trucks and vans)
specs: Odd (1, 3, 5, 7) on the driver side front to back, even (2, 4, 6, 8) on the passenger side
Rear bolts often break, causing a tick at cold start

engines.name: GM EcoTec3 V8 (Gen V: 5.3, 6.2)
specs: Odd (1, 3, 5, 7) on the driver side front to back, even (2, 4, 6, 8) on the passenger side
Direct injection: a high-pressure pump on top of the engine is driven by the camshaft. Never open the high-pressure lines with the engine running
Lifter failures (ticking, misfire, P0300 range) are common on cylinder-deactivation engines
2021 to 2024 6.2L (L87) trucks and SUVs were recalled for engine bearing failure. Check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls

engines.name: GM 4.3 Vortec V6
specs: Has a distributor cap and rotor; replace them with plugs and wires
Lower intake gaskets often leak coolant or oil

engines.name: GM 3800 V6 (3.8)
specs: Lower intake manifold gaskets leak coolant (often into the oil) and the plastic upper intake can crack. Check coolant level often

engines.name: GM 3800 V6 supercharged
specs: The supercharger has its own oil in a small reservoir at the front of the blower
Lower intake manifold gaskets leak coolant. Check coolant level often

engines.name: GM 60-degree V6 (3.1, 3.4)
specs: Very common coolant leak; look for coolant loss and a sweet smell. Milky oil means it is leaking inside

engines.name: GM 3.6 V6
specs: dexos1 (5W-30 on most; some 2018 and newer use 0W-20, check the cap)
Stretch is common on 2007 to 2017 (codes P0008, P0017 and P0016 to P0019, rattle). Long oil change intervals make it worse

engines.name: GM 2.4 Ecotec I4
specs: Many 2010 to 2013 engines burn oil (piston rings), then the timing chain wears from low oil. Check the dipstick at every fill-up

engines.name: GM 1.4 Turbo I4
specs: Built into the valve cover; when it fails you get a whistle, rough idle or oil leaks (rear main seal pushed out). The fix is a new valve cover
Water outlet, thermostat housing and turbo coolant lines leak often

engines.name: GM 6.6 Duramax V8 diesel
specs: 15W-40 diesel oil (API CK-4); dexos D on 2017 and newer
On top of the engine (LB7 to LMM, 2001 to 2010); on the frame rail (LML and L5P, 2011 and newer)
Injectors fail (fuel in the oil, white smoke, rising oil level). A scan tool shows injector balance rates
Has a DPF; LML (2011 on) and L5P also use DEF. Short trips clog the DPF
CP4.2 high-pressure fuel pump can fail and send metal through the fuel system

engines.name: GM 3.0 Duramax I6 diesel
specs: The oil pump is driven by a belt inside the engine; it has a replacement interval in the maintenance schedule

engines.name: GM LS V8 (cars)
specs: Odd (1, 3, 5, 7) on the driver side front to back, even (2, 4, 6, 8) on the passenger side

engines.name: Cadillac Northstar 4.6 V8
specs: Head bolt threads pull out of the aluminum block, causing head gasket failure and overheating. Repair needs thread inserts (engine out)
Lower crankcase (case half) seal leaks oil are common on 2000 and newer

engines.name: Ford 5.4 Triton 3V V8
engines.checked: Oil capacity checked against the factory manual (2007 F-150 5.4)
specs: 1 to 4 on the passenger side front to back, 5 to 8 on the driver side
Two-piece plugs (2004 to 2008) often break in the head. Use Ford's removal procedure (warm engine, small turns, penetrating oil) and a broken-plug extractor if one breaks
Ticking or knocking at idle, codes P0011 / P0021; also timing chain guides and tensioners. Use the right oil and change it on time

engines.name: Ford 4.6 Modular V8
specs: 1 to 4 on the passenger side front to back, 5 to 8 on the driver side
The plastic intake with a coolant crossover cracks at the front on many 1996 to 2001 engines (coolant leak)
2V heads can blow out a plug (few threads); 3V (2005 on) uses two-piece plugs that break on removal

engines.name: Ford 5.0 Coyote V8
specs: 5W-20 or 5W-30 depending on year and model; check the cap
1 to 4 on the passenger side front to back, 5 to 8 on the driver side
Some 2018 and newer engines use oil between changes. Check the dipstick regularly

engines.name: Ford 3.5 EcoBoost V6
engines.checked: Oil capacity checked against the factory manual (2011 F-150 3.5 EcoBoost)
specs: Chain stretch: rattle at startup and codes P0016 to P0019
Loud rattle for a second or two at cold start; Ford issued service bulletins
Stumble or misfire under hard acceleration in humid weather (early F-150s); fixed with a deflector and software

engines.name: Ford 2.7 EcoBoost V6
specs: 2015 to 2017 two-piece composite oil pans leak at the seam

engines.name: Ford 3.5 / 3.7 Duratec V6
specs: In front-wheel-drive models (Edge, Flex, Explorer 2011 on, Taurus, MKX, MKZ, MKS, MKT) the water pump sits inside the engine, driven by the timing chain. A leak sends coolant into the oil: low coolant with no outside leak or milky oil means stop driving

engines.name: Ford 4.0 SOHC V6
specs: Rattle at startup from worn chain guides and tensioners (cassettes). The rear cassette usually means the engine comes out

engines.name: Ford 6.8 Triton V10
specs: Early 2V heads can blow out a plug; 3V (2005 on) uses two-piece plugs that break on removal
Break often, causing a tick and exhaust smell

engines.name: Ford 7.3 Power Stroke V8 diesel
specs: Cam position sensor (CPS) failure stalls it with no warning. Also check the IDM, glow plug relay and the under-valve-cover harness

engines.name: Ford 6.0 Power Stroke V8 diesel
specs: With a scan tool at full warm-up, engine oil temp should be within about 15 F of coolant temp. More than that means a clogged oil cooler, which then kills the EGR cooler
Injector control module should read about 48 V, and stay up while cranking. Low voltage causes hard starts and misfires
Coolant pushed out of the degas bottle under load points to head gaskets / stretched head bolts

engines.name: Ford 6.4 Power Stroke V8 diesel
specs: Radiator leaks, up-pipe leaks, and fuel in the oil from DPF regens. Change oil on time and watch the oil level

engines.name: Ford 6.7 Power Stroke V8 diesel
specs: 10W-30 or 15W-40 meeting Ford spec (check the manual)
2011 to 2019 use the CP4.2 high-pressure pump, which can fail and contaminate the fuel system. Change fuel filters on schedule and use good fuel
DPF and DEF systems; short trips and idling clog the DPF

engines.name: Chrysler 5.7 Hemi V8
engines.checked: Oil capacity checked against the factory manual (2005 Ram 1500 5.7)
specs: Mopar HOAT (2012 and older) or Mopar OAT (2013 and newer); don't mix
Ticking can be broken exhaust manifold bolts (most common, worse cold) or a failing lifter/camshaft on MDS engines (misfire, ticking that stays when warm)

engines.name: Chrysler 6.4 Hemi V8
specs: Lifter and camshaft wear can cause ticking and misfires, like the 5.7

engines.name: Chrysler 3.6 Pentastar V6
specs: 5W-20 (0W-20 on many 2016 and newer; check the cap)
The plastic oil cooler / filter housing between the heads cracks and leaks oil (and sometimes coolant) down the back of the engine
Valve seat wear caused ticking and misfires on one bank; Chrysler extended the warranty on many

engines.name: Chrysler 4.7 PowerTech V8
specs: Overheating can drop a valve seat. Sludge builds up when oil changes are skipped

engines.name: Chrysler 3.7 PowerTech V6
specs: Overheating can drop a valve seat. Keep the cooling system in good shape

engines.name: Cummins 5.9 I6 diesel
specs: On 1989 to 2002 engines a dowel pin behind the timing cover can back out and wreck the gears. A tab kit prevents it
A weak lift pump starves the VP44 injection pump. Check lift pump pressure if it is hard starting or losing power

engines.name: Cummins 6.7 I6 diesel
specs: DPF and EGR from 2007.5; DEF from 2013. Short trips and idling clog the DPF
Hard cold starts can be the intake grid heater or its relay

engines.name: Jeep 4.0 I6
specs: Rear main seal and the oil filter adapter O-rings leak often. Clean and check the adapter first; it is the cheap fix
A failing crankshaft position sensor causes stalling when hot and no-starts

engines.name: Toyota 3.5 V6 (2GR)
specs: 2005 to 2010: a rubber section of the VVT oil cooler line can burst and dump the oil. Toyota replaces it with an all-metal line
Leaks from the weep hole are common; look for pink crust behind the belt

engines.name: Toyota 5.7 V8 (3UR)
specs: Air injection pump or valves fail (P2440, P2442, P2444), often putting it in limp mode after a cold start
Oil seep where the cam towers meet the heads is common

engines.name: Toyota 4.7 V8 (2UZ)
specs: Uses a timing belt: replace about every 90,000 miles, with the water pump and tensioner

engines.name: Toyota 3.0 / 3.3 V6 (1MZ / 3MZ)
specs: Uses a timing belt: replace about every 90,000 miles, with the water pump
1997 to 2002 3.0s can sludge if oil changes are skipped

engines.name: Toyota 2.5 I4 (2AR / A25A)
specs: 0W-20 (some 2018 and newer use 0W-16; check the cap)

engines.name: Toyota 2.4 I4 (2AZ)
specs: Many 2006 to 2011 engines burn oil (piston rings). Check the dipstick at every fill-up
Head bolt threads can pull out of the block, causing coolant loss and overheating

engines.name: Toyota 1.8 I4 (1ZZ / 2ZR)
specs: 1998 to 2002 1ZZ engines often burn oil. Check the dipstick regularly

engines.name: Toyota hybrid (1.8 / 2.0 / 2.5)
specs: Two systems: engine and inverter, each with its own reservoir. Both use Toyota Super Long Life (pink)
Keep the battery cooling vent (by the rear seat) clear of dust and pet hair
A clogged EGR cooler and intake can lead to head gasket failure. Cleaning the EGR system is preventive maintenance
Orange cables are high voltage. Only trained techs should service them

engines.name: Honda 3.5 V6 (J-series)
specs: Uses a timing belt: replace about every 105,000 miles or when the Maintenance Minder shows it (code 4), with the water pump and tensioner
Cylinder deactivation (2008 and newer) can cause oil burning, fouled plugs on the rear bank and broken engine mounts

engines.name: Honda 2.4 I4 (K24)
specs: A grinding rattle for a second at cold start (2008 to 2014) is the VTC actuator on the intake cam
Screw-type adjusters: check valve clearance if it ticks or around 100,000 miles

engines.name: Honda 1.8 I4 (R18)
specs: Some 2006 to 2009 Civic blocks crack and leak coolant (Honda extended the warranty)

engines.name: Honda 1.5 Turbo I4
specs: Fuel can mix into the oil in cold weather (oil level rises, smells like gas). Honda released software updates

engines.name: Nissan V6 (VQ: 3.0, 3.5, 3.7, 4.0)
specs: Crank and cam position sensors were recalled on many Altimas and Maximas for stalling
Some 2003 to 2008 engines burn oil. Check the dipstick regularly

engines.name: Nissan 2.5 I4 (QR25)
specs: The pre-cat can break up and get pulled into the engine, causing oil burning and engine damage
Timing chain; rattle at startup means worn guides or tensioner

engines.name: Hyundai/Kia 2.4 I4 (Theta II)
specs: Connecting rod bearing failure (knocking, stalling, low oil) led to recalls, a knock-sensor software update and extended warranties. Check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls

engines.name: Hyundai/Kia 2.0 Turbo (Theta II)
specs: Connecting rod bearing failure (knocking, stalling, low oil) led to recalls, a knock-sensor software update and extended warranties. Check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls

engines.name: Subaru 2.5 flat-4 (EJ25)
specs: Uses a timing belt: replace about every 105,000 miles, with the idlers, tensioner and water pump
External oil and coolant seeps from the head gaskets are very common (1999 to 2011)

engines.name: Subaru 2.5 Turbo flat-4 (EJ255 / EJ257)
specs: Uses a timing belt: replace about every 105,000 miles
Rod bearing and ringland failures happen; keep the oil full and avoid lugging the engine

engines.name: Subaru 2.0 / 2.5 flat-4 (FB)
specs: Many 2011 to 2015 engines burn oil (Subaru extended the warranty on some). Check the dipstick at every fill-up

engines.name: VW/Audi 2.0 Turbo I4 (EA888)
specs: Use oil with the VW approval in your manual (502 00 on older, 508 00 on newer)
2008 to 2012 engines: the original tensioner can fail and let the chain jump, wrecking the engine. Check which tensioner it has
A torn PCV diaphragm causes a whistle, rough idle and lean codes
The plastic water pump / thermostat housing leaks often (pink crust on the passenger side)
Direct injection: intake valves build carbon; walnut blasting cleans them

engines.name: VW/Audi 1.8 Turbo I4 (1999 to 2006)
specs: Synthetic meeting VW 502 00 (the engine can sludge on conventional oil)
Interference engine with a timing belt; follow the interval in the manual and replace the tensioner too
Coil packs fail (misfire); many were replaced under a recall

engines.name: VW 2.5 I5
specs: The timing chain is at the back of the engine (transmission side); replacing it is a big job

engines.name: VW/Audi TDI diesel (1.9 / 2.0)
specs: Interference engine with a timing belt; follow the interval in the manual
The high-pressure fuel pump can fail and send metal through the fuel system. Use only diesel; one tank of gas can destroy it

engines.name: BMW inline-6
specs: BMW Longlife approved oil (see the manual)
Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak (oil on the belt or burning smell)
Water pump and thermostat fail without warning on many; use BMW coolant (blue)

engines.name: BMW 3.0 Turbo inline-6 (N54 / N55 / B58)
specs: BMW Longlife approved oil (see the manual)
High-pressure fuel pump, injectors and wastegate rattle are common
Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak (oil on the belt or burning smell)
Electric water pump and thermostat fail without warning on N54/N55

engines.name: BMW 2.0 Turbo I4 (N20 / B46)
specs: Timing chain guides wear and break (whine or rattle). Have it checked; failure ruins the engine

engines.name: Ford 5.4 Triton 2V V8
specs: 1 to 4 on the passenger side front to back, 5 to 8 on the driver side
The 2V heads have few threads; a plug can blow out. Torque plugs to spec and don't over-tighten

engines.name: Ford 4.2 V6 (Essex)
specs: Intake and front cover gaskets can leak coolant, sometimes into the oil. Check for milky oil and coolant loss

engines.name: Chrysler 2.7 V6
specs: Very prone to sludge; change oil on time with the right grade
The water pump is inside the engine, driven by the timing chain. A failure puts coolant in the oil: milky oil or coolant loss means stop driving

engines.name: Chrysler 3.5 V6
specs: Uses a timing belt; follow the interval in the manual and replace the water pump with it

engines.name: Toyota 3.4 V6 (5VZ)
specs: Uses a timing belt: replace about every 90,000 miles, with the water pump

engines.name: Inline 4-cylinder
specs: 1-3-4-2 on almost every inline 4-cylinder (cylinder 1 is at the timing belt or chain end)

engines.name: Electric vehicle
specs: None. No oil changes, spark plugs or timing belts
The battery and motor have their own coolant loop; use only the maker's coolant
A weak 12 V battery can stop an EV from turning on, even with a full main battery
Regenerative braking means pads last long, but calipers can rust from lack of use. Brake fluid still needs changing
Orange cables are high voltage. Only trained techs should service them
6.0 gas with an automatic: 4L80-E, about 7.7 qt for a pan drop (factory manual, 2004 Silverado 2500). Duramax and 8.1: Allison 1000

gm_4l60e: 1500 models with an automatic: 4L60-E / 4L65-E. Fluid: Dexron VI (replaces Dexron III). About 5 qt for a pan drop and filter; check hot, in Park, engine running
ford_10r80: If it has the 10-speed automatic (2017 and newer): Mercon ULV fluid only. No dipstick; the level is checked at a plug at operating temperature (shop job)
honda_9speed: If it has the 9-speed automatic (push-button shifter): rough shifts were improved with dealer software updates
nissan_cvt: If it has a CVT: Nissan NS-2 or NS-3 fluid only (depends on year); the wrong fluid damages it
subaru_cvt: If it has the Lineartronic CVT: use only Subaru CVT fluid
fca_9speed: If it has the 9-speed automatic: rough shifts were improved with dealer software updates
vw_dsg: If it has a 6-speed DSG automatic: fluid and filter change about every 40,000 miles
